entries.name: ArteraAI Prostate
entries.tagline: Prognostic AI test using digital pathology images for prostate cancer.

regulatory.detail: De Novo granted 2025-07-31 (DEN240068). Product code SFH — pathology software algorithm device analysing digital images for cancer prognosis.

entries.summary: Prognostic algorithm analysing digitised prostate biopsy images alongside clinical variables to inform risk assessment and therapy decisions. Created the SFH product code for prognostic pathology algorithms.

entries.clinician_note: A no-frills slide viewer. Opens big scanner files quickly and lets you draw regions.
entries.name: ASAP
entries.tagline: Fast whole-slide image viewer with annotation support.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Lightweight viewer for multi-resolution whole-slide images with a simple annotation workflow, widely used to inspect and label slides for challenge datasets.

entries.clinician_note: Research-focused. Useful if you want the academic papers rather than usable tools.
entries.name: Awesome-Pathology-VLMs
entries.tagline: Curated list of pathology vision-language models, datasets and benchmarks.
entries.summary: Focused bibliography of pathology vision-language models organised by training paradigm, with a useful patch/ROI/WSI granularity axis. A good deep reference for the VLM literature specifically.

entries.licence_notes: Published document; check the publisher's terms for reuse.
entries.name: Predicting Acquisition Site from TCGA Images
entries.tagline: Independent confirmation that acquisition site leaks into the pixels.
entries.summary: Demonstrates that networks can identify which institution produced a TCGA slide, reinforcing that site is a confounder that must be controlled in study design rather than assumed away.

entries.name: CAMELYON16
entries.tagline: Lymph node metastasis detection challenge dataset.
entries.summary: Sentinel lymph node whole-slide images with exhaustive metastasis annotations. The reference benchmark for weakly and fully supervised WSI detection.

entries.clinician_note: The reason synoptic reporting exists: every element you fill in becomes a field a registry or a trial can actually use.
entries.name: CAP electronic Cancer Checklists (eCC)
entries.tagline: Machine-readable cancer synoptic reporting protocols.
entries.summary: Machine-readable XML encoding of the CAP cancer case summaries, structured as coded question-and-answer pairs so synoptic reports become queryable data rather than prose. SNOMED CT encoded since 2007.

entries.licence_notes: Published document; check the publisher's terms for reuse.
entries.clinician_note: If your laboratory is going digital, this is the document your validation study will be judged against. Read it before you buy a scanner, not after.
entries.name: CAP Guideline — Validating Whole Slide Imaging
entries.tagline: The reference guideline for validating a WSI system for diagnostic use.
entries.summary: Evidence-based guidance from CAP, with ASCP and the Association for Pathology Informatics, on how a laboratory should validate a whole slide imaging system before using it for diagnosis. Originally issued 2013 and updated in 2021 using the GRADE framework.

entries.licence_notes: Check the repository before any reuse.
entries.clinician_note: Usable from QuPath via an extension if you would rather not touch Python.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.name: Cellpose
entries.tagline: Generalist cell and nucleus segmentation across imaging modalities.
entries.summary: Widely used generalist segmentation model that works across many microscopy types without retraining, with a human-in-the-loop retraining workflow when it does not.

entries.name: CellViT
entries.tagline: Vision-transformer nucleus segmentation and classification.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Transformer-based nucleus instance segmentation built on pretrained ViT encoders, with inference tooling for scaling detection across whole slides.

entries.licence_notes: Published document; check the publisher's terms for reuse.
entries.name: CLAIM
entries.tagline: Checklist for artificial intelligence in medical imaging.
entries.summary: Reporting checklist aimed specifically at medical imaging AI, covering data handling, ground truth definition, model description and evaluation. Widely requested by imaging journals at submission.

entries.name: CLAM
entries.tagline: Attention-based multiple-instance learning for weakly supervised whole-slide classification.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Widely used reference implementation of attention-based MIL for slide-level classification from slide-level labels only, with heatmap interpretability. The default baseline in most WSI classification papers.

entries.licence_notes: Check the repository and model card before any reuse.
entries.clinician_note: Worth knowing about because it takes seriously a problem most benchmarks ignore: whether a model can score well without actually looking at the slide.
entries.name: CleanSlide
entries.tagline: Leakage-audited pan-cancer whole-slide multiple-choice benchmark.
entries.summary: TCGA-derived benchmark of about 149,000 four-option questions over 9,985 diagnostic slides, with train/validation/test splits disjoint by patient AND by tissue source site, and a blind image-free baseline reported for every task.

entries.licence_notes: Gated on Hugging Face; non-commercial research terms.
entries.name: CONCH
entries.tagline: Vision-language foundation model for pathology image-text tasks.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Contrastively pretrained image-text model for pathology supporting zero-shot classification, cross-modal retrieval, captioning and segmentation.

entries.licence_notes: Published document; check the publisher's terms for reuse.
entries.name: CONSORT-AI and SPIRIT-AI
entries.tagline: Trial reporting and protocol guidelines for AI interventions.
entries.summary: Extensions of the CONSORT and SPIRIT statements for randomised trials evaluating interventions that include an AI component, published together in Nature Medicine.

entries.licence_notes: Check the repository and model card before any reuse.
entries.name: CPath-Omni
entries.tagline: Unified multimodal model spanning patch and whole-slide analysis.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Attempts to handle patch-level and slide-level tasks in a single model rather than training separate systems for each scale.

entries.licence_notes: Check the repository and model card before any reuse.
entries.name: CPathAgent
entries.tagline: Agent that navigates a slide the way a pathologist moves a microscope.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Models the zoom-and-pan behaviour of slide review as agent actions, unifying patch, region and slide-level capability in one system and reporting an interpretable trajectory of what it looked at.

entries.clinician_note: Runs on a server your institution controls, so several people can annotate the same slides in a browser. Needs IT support to set up.
entries.caveats: Self-hosting requires a server and maintenance; not a laptop tool.
entries.name: Cytomine
entries.tagline: Web-based collaborative platform for annotating and analysing whole-slide images.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Server-hosted platform for multi-user slide annotation, review and analysis, designed for collaborative projects and teaching cohorts.

entries.licence_notes: Published document; check the publisher's terms for reuse.
entries.clinician_note: The stage most pathology AI has never been through. Worth asking a vendor whether their product has.
entries.name: DECIDE-AI
entries.tagline: Reporting guideline for early live clinical evaluation of AI decision support.
entries.summary: Covers the stage between offline validation and a full trial — the first time an AI system is used by real clinicians on real patients — with emphasis on safety and human factors rather than accuracy alone.

entries.licence_notes: Check the repository before any reuse.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.name: DeepSpot
entries.tagline: Uses spatial context from surrounding tissue to improve expression prediction.
entries.summary: Predicts spot-level expression from H&E while explicitly modelling the neighbouring tissue context rather than treating each tile independently.

entries.clinician_note: Ask an AI vendor how their results are stored. If the answer is a bespoke database, your results are locked in.
entries.name: DICOM Structured Reporting
entries.tagline: Encoding measurements and findings as structured DICOM objects.
entries.summary: The mechanism for storing AI outputs — measurements, annotations, findings — as structured objects alongside the image rather than as a separate proprietary file.

entries.licence_notes: Open standard published by NEMA; the specification is free to read.
entries.clinician_note: The reason a slide from one scanner can be opened by another vendor's software. Ask about DICOM support before buying anything.
entries.name: DICOM for Whole Slide Imaging
entries.tagline: The vendor-neutral standard for storing and exchanging pathology slides.
entries.summary: The DICOM VL Whole Slide Microscopy Image IOD defines how scanned slides are represented, enabling storage and exchange independent of scanner vendor.

entries.name: Digital Slide Archive
entries.tagline: Server platform for managing, annotating and analysing large slide collections.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Web platform built on Girder for organising whole-slide image collections, with annotation tooling and a plugin system for running analysis jobs at scale.

entries.licence_notes: Published document; check the publisher's terms for reuse.
entries.clinician_note: A good starting point if your department is considering going digital and wants peer experience rather than vendor material.
entries.name: Digital Pathology Association
entries.tagline: Professional body publishing practical digital pathology guidance.
entries.summary: Professional association publishing white papers, webinars and practical guidance on adopting digital pathology, including validation and telepathology workflows.

entries.licence_notes: Check the repository and model card before any reuse.
entries.name: Dr-LLaVA
entries.tagline: Instruction tuning grounded in symbolic clinical reasoning.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Constrains a vision-language assistant with symbolic representations of clinical reasoning steps, so that its answers follow a defensible diagnostic sequence rather than arriving at conclusions unaccountably.

entries.licence_notes: Check the repository and model card before any reuse.
entries.name: EAGLE
entries.tagline: Preference alignment to reduce hallucination in pathology VLMs.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Builds a large set of preferred and rejected response pairs and applies iterative preference optimisation, targeting multimodal hallucination and biased answers — a failure mode that matters more in pathology than in general vision tasks.

entries.licence_notes: Published document; check the publisher's terms for reuse.
entries.clinician_note: 'CE marked' under the old directive and under IVDR are not the same claim. Check which one a vendor means.
entries.name: EU IVDR 2017/746
entries.tagline: The regulation governing in vitro diagnostic devices in the European Union.
entries.summary: Full legal text of the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation, which governs CE marking for diagnostic software including pathology algorithms, and which reclassified much software upward in risk class compared with the previous directive.

entries.licence_notes: Published document; check the publisher's terms for reuse.

entries.name: Good Machine Learning Practice for Medical Device Development
entries.tagline: Ten guiding principles agreed by the FDA, Health Canada and the MHRA.
entries.summary: Joint statement of ten principles covering data quality, representativeness, training and test independence, human factors and lifecycle monitoring for medical-device machine learning.

entries.licence_notes: Published document; check the publisher's terms for reuse.
entries.name: FDA Predetermined Change Control Plans for AI Devices
entries.tagline: How a cleared AI device may be updated without a new submission.
entries.summary: FDA guidance on describing, in advance, the modifications an AI-enabled device may undergo after clearance and how they will be validated — the mechanism that makes a continuously-learning device regulable at all.

entries.licence_notes: Check the repository before any reuse.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.name: GHIST
entries.tagline: Single-cell resolution spatial gene expression from histology.
entries.summary: Predicts spatially resolved expression at single-cell rather than spot resolution, using cell segmentation alongside image features.

entries.licence_notes: Check the repository before any reuse.
entries.clinician_note: Run this before trusting any result computed on a batch of scanned slides. Most 'model failure' turns out to be slide quality.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.name: GrandQC
entries.tagline: Tissue detection and multi-class artefact segmentation for whole slides.
entries.summary: Segments tissue and the common artefacts that ruin downstream analysis — tissue folds, pen marks, bubbles, edges, black spots, foreign objects and out-of-focus regions. Released with a manually annotated test set and QC masks for all of TCGA.

entries.licence_notes: Published document; check the publisher's terms for reuse.
entries.clinician_note: A realistic entry point for a department that cannot justify a bulk scanner. Small enough to sit on a desk.
entries.caveats: Regulatory status varies by model and jurisdiction and was NOT verified against a primary regulator record for this entry — confirm before any diagnostic use.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.name: Grundium Ocus
entries.tagline: Portable single-slide scanner at a fraction of the cost of a bulk system.
entries.summary: Compact desktop scanner handling one slide at a time, aimed at telepathology, consultation, case documentation and teaching rather than high-volume clinical throughput.

entries.licence_notes: Free to use; content is copyrighted by its publisher.
entries.clinician_note: Practical rather than clever — the sort of thing that saves ten minutes a day.
entries.name: Hematogones.com
entries.tagline: Free browser tools and synoptic reporting templates for laboratory work.
entries.summary: Collection of browser-based calculators, cancer-protocol synoptic templates and reporting work aids, aimed at reducing the clerical load of report generation.

entries.licence_notes: Aggregates many source datasets, each with its own terms.
entries.name: HEST-1k / HEST-Bench
entries.tagline: Paired histology and spatial transcriptomics dataset and benchmark.
entries.summary: Harmonised collection of spatial transcriptomics profiles paired with histology, plus a benchmark for predicting expression from morphology.

entries.licence_notes: Check the repository before any reuse.

entries.tagline: Transformer and graph approaches to expression prediction from histology.
entries.summary: Two closely related lines of work applying vision transformers, and transformers combined with graph neural networks, to predict spatial expression from histology spots — modelling relationships between spots rather than each in isolation.

entries.name: HistomicsTK
entries.tagline: Python toolkit for histology image analysis and feature extraction.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Library of histology-specific image analysis routines — colour deconvolution, stain normalisation, nucleus detection and morphometric feature extraction — usable standalone or as the analysis layer behind Digital Slide Archive.

entries.clinician_note: Checks a batch of scanned slides for problems like blur or pen marks before anyone spends time on them.
entries.name: HistoQC
entries.tagline: Automated quality control for whole-slide images.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Pipeline that flags slide artefacts — blur, pen marks, tissue folds, coverslip edges, bubbles — and produces an interactive report for triaging a cohort before analysis.

entries.clinician_note: If a vendor cannot tell you how their output reaches your LIS, this is the vocabulary in which to ask the question.
entries.name: HL7 FHIR
entries.tagline: The interoperability standard for exchanging health data, including reports.
entries.summary: Resource-based standard for health data exchange. DiagnosticReport, Specimen, Observation and ImagingStudy are the resources a pathology system needs to speak to the rest of the hospital.

entries.name: HoVer-Net
entries.tagline: Simultaneous nucleus segmentation and classification in histology.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Network predicting horizontal and vertical distances to nuclear centres to separate touching nuclei, while simultaneously classifying nucleus type. A standard baseline for nucleus tasks.

entries.licence_notes: Check the repository before any reuse.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.name: HoVer-NeXt
entries.tagline: Faster successor to HoVer-Net for nucleus segmentation and classification.
entries.summary: Reimplementation aimed at making whole-slide nucleus segmentation and classification tractable at scale rather than on selected tiles.

entries.clinician_note: Runs after you have signed out, and raises a flag if it disagrees. Designed as a safety net, not a first opinion.
entries.caveats: Clearance is specific to the indication for use stated in the FDA record and to the United States. It implies nothing about availability or approval elsewhere. Verify the current indication and your own jurisdiction's status before clinical use.
entries.name: Ibex Galen Second Read
entries.tagline: AI second-read quality control for biopsy whole-slide images.

regulatory.detail: 510(k) cleared 2025-01-24 (K241232). Product code QPN — software algorithm device to assist users in digital pathology.

entries.summary: Software that reviews already-diagnosed cases and flags discrepancies between the algorithm's assessment and the recorded diagnosis, intended as a quality-control second read rather than a primary diagnostic step.

entries.name: ICD-O-3
entries.tagline: Topography and morphology coding for cancer registries.
entries.summary: WHO classification coding tumour site and morphology, the coding backbone of cancer registration worldwide.

entries.caveats: Not free. Budget for it if you intend to build a regulated product.
entries.name: IEC 62304
entries.tagline: International standard for medical device software lifecycle processes.
entries.summary: Defines the lifecycle requirements for medical device software: planning, requirements, architecture, verification, release and maintenance, scaled by safety class.

entries.caveats: Clearance is specific to the indication for use stated in the FDA record and to the United States. It implies nothing about availability or approval elsewhere. Verify the current indication and your own jurisdiction's status before clinical use.
entries.name: Indica Labs HALO AP Dx
entries.tagline: Anatomic pathology workflow and image analysis platform.

regulatory.detail: 510(k) cleared 2025-11-25 (K252762) as digital pathology image viewing and management software (QKQ); earlier clearance K232833 in 2024 as a whole slide imaging system (PSY).

entries.summary: Case management and viewing platform for anatomic pathology, from a company whose research image-analysis software is widely used in academic laboratories.

entries.licence_notes: Check the repository before any reuse.

entries.name: InstanSeg
entries.tagline: Embedding-based cell segmentation that runs acceptably on a CPU.
entries.summary: Instance segmentation approach designed for speed, able to run without a dedicated GPU — which matters more than raw accuracy when there is no workstation available.

entries.licence_notes: The standard must be purchased.
entries.caveats: Not free.
entries.name: ISO 14971
entries.tagline: Risk management standard for medical devices.
entries.summary: The framework regulators expect for identifying hazards, estimating risk and showing that residual risk is acceptable. Underpins nearly every other device requirement.

entries.licence_notes: Check the repository before any reuse.
entries.clinician_note: The idea worth knowing: morphology carries enough signal to interpolate molecular data between measured points — but it is inference, not measurement.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.name: iStar
entries.tagline: Super-resolution spatial gene expression from histology and spatial transcriptomics.
entries.summary: Uses hierarchical image features to integrate spatial transcriptomics with high-resolution histology, raising expression predictions towards near-single-cell resolution rather than the coarse spots the assay produces.

entries.licence_notes: Published document; check the publisher's terms for reuse.
entries.clinician_note: Read this before trusting any performance figure. Most published accuracy is measured under conditions that do not resemble a working laboratory.
entries.caveats: Maintained by this project rather than drawn from a single source; each failure mode links to its own primary literature.
entries.name: Known Failure Modes in Pathology AI
entries.tagline: A plain-language index of how these systems actually go wrong.
entries.summary: Curated index of documented failure modes: site and batch confounding, scanner and stain variability, distribution shift after deployment, miscalibrated confidence, hallucinated findings in generative models, and automation bias in the reader.

entries.clinician_note: The scanner itself, not an AI tool — it produces the digital slides everything else works on.
entries.caveats: Clearance is specific to the indication for use stated in the FDA record and to the United States. It implies nothing about availability or approval elsewhere. Verify the current indication and your own jurisdiction's status before clinical use.
entries.name: Leica Aperio GT 450 DX
entries.tagline: Whole-slide scanner cleared for primary diagnosis.

regulatory.detail: 510(k) cleared 2024-04-16 (K232202). Product code PSY — whole slide imaging system.

entries.summary: High-throughput brightfield whole-slide scanner and associated software cleared as a whole slide imaging system for diagnostic use.

entries.licence_notes: Check the repository and model card before any reuse.
entries.caveats: Biomedical-general rather than pathology-specific; histopathology is a minority of its training data.
entries.name: LLaVA-Med
entries.tagline: Biomedical vision-language assistant trained rapidly from PubMed figures.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: General biomedical multimodal assistant covering many imaging modalities including histopathology. Frequently used as the baseline that pathology-specific assistants are compared against.

entries.name: LOINC
entries.tagline: Universal codes for laboratory observations and report sections.
entries.summary: Naming system for tests, measurements and document sections, used alongside SNOMED CT so that the question and the answer are both coded.

entries.licence_notes: Check the repository before any reuse.
entries.clinician_note: Mitotic count drives grading in several tumours, and it is one of the least reproducible things pathologists do — which is exactly why this benchmark measures generalisation rather than headline accuracy.
entries.name: MIDOG Challenge
entries.tagline: Mitosis detection benchmarked across scanners, tumours and species.
entries.summary: Challenge series built specifically around domain shift: models must count mitoses on scanners, tumour types and species they were not trained on. Successive editions have widened the domain gap deliberately.

entries.licence_notes: Check the repository and model card before any reuse.
entries.name: MUSK
entries.tagline: Vision-language foundation model for precision oncology.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Trained on large volumes of unpaired image and text data as well as paired examples, then applied to retrieval, visual question answering, classification and molecular biomarker prediction.

entries.clinician_note: A good starting dataset if you are learning — small enough to work with on a laptop.
entries.name: NCT-CRC-HE-100K
entries.tagline: Colorectal tissue-type patch classification dataset.
entries.summary: Around 100,000 colorectal H&E patches labelled into nine tissue classes. Small, permissively licensed and CPU-tractable, which makes it the usual first dataset for teaching and prototyping.

entries.clinician_note: Matters if slides are going to the cloud — proprietary scanner formats were not designed for that.
entries.name: OME-Zarr / NGFF
entries.tagline: Cloud-native chunked format for bioimaging, including whole slides.
entries.summary: Next-generation file format storing large multi-resolution images as chunked arrays, designed to be read efficiently from object storage rather than a local disk.

entries.name: OMERO
entries.tagline: Image data management server for microscopy, including whole-slide images.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Long-established server and client suite for storing, annotating and sharing microscopy image data across many proprietary formats.

entries.licence_notes: Open hardware licence; the software is separately open-source.
entries.clinician_note: The genuinely low-cost option. You print the body, add optics and a Raspberry Pi, and get automated scanning for telepathology or teaching.
entries.caveats: Not a diagnostic device, and image quality does not match a commercial scanner. Appropriate for education, documentation and second opinions rather than primary diagnosis.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.name: OpenFlexure Microscope
entries.tagline: Open-source 3D-printed automated microscope for low-resource settings.
entries.summary: 3D-printable motorised microscope that automates scanning and stitches composite images viewable on a laptop, tablet or phone. Designed explicitly for settings where a commercial scanner is out of reach.

entries.name: OpenSlide
entries.tagline: C library with Python bindings for reading proprietary whole-slide formats.
entries.summary: The foundational library for reading vendor whole-slide formats (Aperio, Hamamatsu, Leica, MIRAX and others) through one common interface. Most Python pathology tooling depends on it.

entries.licence_notes: Published document; check the publisher's terms for reuse.
entries.caveats: A research design rather than a product; building it requires hardware skills.

entries.licence_notes: Check the repository before any reuse.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.name: PathAgent

entries.name: PathChat
